# Strings

## Introduction

Strings in Blueberry are mutable byte arrays. Not UTF-8 codepoints — individual bytes are plain integers.
General philosophy is, unlike in many scripting languages, strings represent memory, not a value type.
Copy is explicit, with ability to preallocate size.

### Immutable literals

String literals in source code are **read-only**. They live in static memory and cannot be modified:

```javascript
var s = "hello"
s.append(" world")   // error: string is read-only
```

Literals are deduplicated — equal literals always resolve to the same pointer, so `==` works for interned strings:

```javascript
var s1 = "hello"
var s2 = "hello"   // even if loaded from another file

if (s1 == s2) {
    print("is true")   // pointer identity, works for literals
}

var mutable = "hel".copy().append("lo")

if (s1 != mutable) {
    print("== compares by pointer, not byte content")
}

if (string.eq(s1, mutable)) {
    print("equal")   // byte-value comparison
}

if (s2.eq(mutable)) {
    print("equal")
}
```

### Mutable strings and the copy pattern

To get a mutable string from a literal, call `.copy()`. This allocates a new writable string with the same content:

```javascript
var s = "hello".copy()
s.append(" world")   // ok — s is now "hello world"
```

Mutation methods return `self`, so they can be chained:

```javascript
var s = "  Hello  ".copy().trim().lower()   // "hello"
```

### Creating strings from scratch

Use `string.new(size?)` to allocate an empty mutable string with preallocated capacity. The string starts empty but the buffer is immediately reserved — no reallocation will happen until you exceed `size` bytes. Default capacity is 64.

```javascript
var s = string.new(64)
s.append("host: ").append(hostname).append("\r\n")
```

### Slices

A slice is a zero-copy view into a parent string, created with `.__slice()`. Slices share memory with their parent and involve no allocation — useful for parsing. `.slice()` (without the `__`) always produces an independent copy.

---

## `string` namespace

### `string.new(size?)`

Allocate a new empty mutable string. `size` bytes are immediately reserved — the buffer is preallocated upfront, not lazily. Default is 64. The string starts empty; use `.append()` to fill it.

```javascript
var s = string.new(128)
s.append("hello")
```

### `string.format(fmt, args...)` / `string.printf`

Create a new formatted string. See [Format Strings](#format-strings) for specifiers.

```javascript
var s = string.format("x = %d, y = %d", x, y)
```

### `string.eq(a, b)`

Byte-value equality between two strings. Returns `null` if either argument is not a string.

```javascript
string.eq("hello", "hello")   // true
string.eq("hello", 42)        // null
```

### `string.cmp(a, b)`

Lexicographic comparison. Returns `-1`, `0`, or `1`. Returns `null` if either argument is not a string.

```javascript
string.cmp("abc", "abd")   // -1
```

---

## Object Methods

All string values share a built-in prototype. Methods are called with dot syntax. Mutation methods require a writable string and return `self` for chaining.

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `.len()` | Length in bytes |
| `.size()` | Allocated buffer capacity in bytes |
| `.size(n)` | Preallocate `n` additional bytes of tail space, return self |
| `.is_readonly()` | True if string is immutable |
| `.is_slice()` | True if string is a zero-copy slice view |
| `.at(idx)` / `.get(idx)` | Byte at index as int, `null` if out of bounds |
| `.set(idx, byte)` | Set byte at index, returns self |
| `.slice(start, end?)` | New copy of substring |
| `.__slice(start, end?)` | Zero-copy view into parent |
| `.slice_offset()` | Byte offset of slice within parent |
| `.parent()` | Owning string of a slice |
| `.ctx()` | Context pointer stored on a slice |
| `.find(needle, start?)` | Index of first match, or `false` |
| `.contains(needle)` | True if needle found anywhere |
| `.starts(prefix)` | True if string starts with prefix |
| `.ends(suffix)` | True if string ends with suffix |
| `.append(other)` | Append in place, return self |
| `.prepend(other)` | Prepend in place, return self |
| `.clear()` | Reset length to 0, return self |
| `.upper()` | ASCII uppercase in place, return self |
| `.lower()` | ASCII lowercase in place, return self |
| `.trim()` | Strip leading/trailing whitespace in place, return self |
| `.rev()` | Reverse in place, return self |
| `.copy()` | New independent mutable copy |
| `.repeat(n)` | New string repeated n times |
| `.replace(needle, repl)` | New string with all occurrences replaced |
| `.split(delim)` | Array of strings split on delimiter |
| `.bytes()` | Array of byte values as ints |
| `.eq(other)` | Byte-value equality, `null` if other is not a string |
| `.cmp(other)` | Lexicographic compare: `-1`/`0`/`1`, `null` if not a string |
| `.hash()` | FNV-1a hash as int |
| `.format(fmt, args...)` | Append formatted content, return self |
| `.printf(fmt, args...)` | Alias for `.format()` |

---

### `.len()`

Returns the length of the string in bytes.

```javascript
"hello".len()   // 5
```

### `.size(n?)`

With no argument, returns the allocated buffer capacity in bytes (always `>= .len()`).

With an integer argument, preallocates `n` additional bytes of tail space and returns self. This is a forward declaration of intent — "I plan to append `n` more bytes" — and avoids reallocation during subsequent appends. The string length does not change.

```javascript
var s = string.new()
s.size(4096)   // reserve 4096 more bytes now
s.append(big_chunk)   // no realloc needed
```

### `.is_readonly()`

Returns `true` if the string is immutable (e.g. a string literal). Mutation methods will error on read-only strings.

### `.is_slice()`

Returns `true` if this string is a zero-copy slice view into a parent string.

---

### `.at(idx)` / `.get(idx)`

Returns the byte at `idx` as an integer. Negative indices wrap from the end. Returns `null` if out of bounds.

```javascript
"hello".at(0)    // 104  ('h')
"hello".at(-1)   // 111  ('o')
```

Strings also support index syntax: `s[i]` calls `.at(i)`.

### `.set(idx, byte)`

Sets the byte at `idx` to `byte` (an integer). Negative indices wrap. Errors if out of bounds or string is read-only. Returns self.

```javascript
var s = "hello".copy()
s.set(0, 72)   // 'H'
s[0] = 72      // same via index syntax
```

### `.slice(start, end?)`

Returns a new independent copy of the substring `[start, end)`. Negative indices wrap. If `end` is omitted, slices to the end of the string.

```javascript
"hello world".slice(6)     // "world"
"hello world".slice(0, 5)  // "hello"
"hello".slice(-3)           // "llo"
```

### `.__slice(start, end?)`

Zero-copy view into the parent string. The returned string shares memory with its parent — no allocation, but the parent must outlive the slice. Useful for parsing.

### `.slice_offset()`

For a slice, returns the byte offset of this slice's start within the parent string's buffer. Returns `null` if not a slice, `0` if parent is static memory.

### `.parent()`

For a slice, returns the owning parent string. Returns `null` for non-slices.

### `.ctx()`

For a slice, returns the arbitrary context pointer stored on it. Returns `null` for non-slices.

---

### `.find(needle, start?)`

Returns the index of the first occurrence of `needle` starting from `start` (default 0). Negative `start` wraps. Returns `false` if not found.

```javascript
"hello world".find("world")   // 6
"hello world".find("xyz")     // false
"abcabc".find("bc", 2)        // 4
```

### `.contains(needle)`

Returns `true` if `needle` occurs anywhere in the string.

```javascript
"hello world".contains("world")   // true
```

### `.starts(prefix)`

Returns `true` if the string starts with `prefix`.

```javascript
"hello".starts("he")   // true
```

### `.ends(suffix)`

Returns `true` if the string ends with `suffix`.

```javascript
"hello".ends("lo")   // true
```

---

### `.append(other)`

Appends `other` to the end of the string. Returns self.

```javascript
var s = string.new()
s.append("hello").append(" world")
```

### `.prepend(other)`

Prepends `other` to the beginning of the string. Returns self.

```javascript
var s = "world".copy()
s.prepend("hello ")   // "hello world"
```

### `.clear()`

Removes all content, resetting length to 0. Capacity is retained. Returns self.

### `.upper()`

Converts all ASCII letters to uppercase in place. Returns self.

```javascript
"hello".copy().upper()   // "HELLO"
```

### `.lower()`

Converts all ASCII letters to lowercase in place. Returns self.

### `.trim()`

Removes leading and trailing whitespace (`' '`, `'\t'`, `'\n'`, `'\r'`) in place. Returns self.

```javascript
"  hello  ".copy().trim()   // "hello"
```

### `.rev()`

Reverses the string in place. Returns self.

```javascript
"hello".copy().rev()   // "olleh"
```

---

### `.copy()`

Returns a new independent mutable copy of the string.

```javascript
var s = "hello".copy()
s.append(" world")
```

### `.repeat(n)`

Returns a new string with the content repeated `n` times. Returns `""` if `n <= 0`.

```javascript
"ab".repeat(3)   // "ababab"
```

### `.replace(needle, replacement)`

Returns a new string with all occurrences of `needle` replaced by `replacement`. The original is not modified.

```javascript
"hello world".replace("world", "there")   // "hello there"
```

---

### `.split(delim)`

Splits the string on `delim` and returns an array of strings. If `delim` is `""`, splits into individual bytes as single-character strings.

```javascript
"a,b,c".split(",")   // ["a", "b", "c"]
"hi".split("")        // ["h", "i"]
```

### `.bytes()`

Returns an array of integers, one per byte.

```javascript
"hi".bytes()   // [104, 105]
```

---

### `.eq(other)`

Byte-value string equality. Returns `null` if either argument is not a string (does not throw).

```javascript
"hello".eq("hello")   // true
"hello".eq("world")   // false
"hello".eq(42)        // null
```

### `.cmp(other)`

Lexicographic comparison. Returns `-1`, `0`, or `1`. Returns `null` if either argument is not a string.

```javascript
"abc".cmp("abd")   // -1
"abc".cmp("abc")   // 0
"abd".cmp("abc")   // 1
```

### `.hash()`

Returns the FNV-1a hash of the string as an integer.

---

## Format Strings

`.format(fmt, args...)` appends formatted output to the string in place and returns self. When called as `string.format(...)`, a new string is created instead. `.printf` is an alias for `.format`.

```javascript
// method style — appends to existing string
var s = string.new()
s.format("x=%d, name=%s", 42, "bob")

// namespace style — creates new string
var s = string.format("x=%d, name=%s", 42, "bob")

// chaining
var s = string.new(64)
s.format("[%s", "start").format("|%d", 42).format("|%x]", 0xFF)
// "[start|42|ff]"
```

### Specifiers

| Specifier | Argument | Output |
|-----------|----------|--------|
| `%d` / `%i` | int or float (truncated) | Decimal integer |
| `%u` | int | Unsigned decimal |
| `%x` | int | Hex lowercase (`ff`) |
| `%X` | int | Hex uppercase (`FF`) |
| `%o` | int | Octal |
| `%b` | int | Binary |
| `%f` | float | Decimal float (default 6 places) |
| `%e` | float | Scientific notation (`1.5e10`) |
| `%g` | float | Shorter of decimal or scientific |
| `%s` | string | String value; int/float printed as number |
| `%c` | int | UTF-8 encoded codepoint |
| `%%` | — | Literal `%` |

Width, precision, alignment, and zero-padding are supported: `%10d`, `%-10s`, `%.4f`, `%08x`, `%020e`.

### Type mismatches

The formatter never crashes on wrong types — it emits a placeholder instead:

| Situation | Output |
|-----------|--------|
| `%d`/`%x`/`%o`/`%b`/`%f`/`%e`/`%g` with non-number | `<!NUM>` |
| `%s` with non-string, non-number | `<!STR>` |
| `%c` with non-integer | `<!CHR>` |
| Missing argument | `<!ARG>` |

```javascript
string.format("%d", "hello")   // "<!NUM>"
string.format("%s", null)      // "<!STR>"
string.format("%d")            // "<!ARG>"
string.format("100%%")         // "100%"
```
